findings.source: L1AtomicTokenBridgeCreator.createTokenBridge: creation code buffers (type(...).creationCode, template.code) and abi.encode of constructor arguments
findings.issue: Memory positions after several dynamic allocations are printed as nested floor32/ceil32 sums (312 lines), so the constructor-argument buffers cannot be followed.
findings.rule: Bind each allocation result (mem[64] after an allocation) to a named temporary and print later addresses relative to it.

findings.issue: The same salt computation prints as sha3('L1R', Bytes(20, _param1)) for one proxy and as a hash of raw memory (with the 'L1SGW' literal in hex and a dead store) for the next, because the free-memory pointer is unknown there.
findings.rule: Resolve sha3(mem[p len n]) whenever the words in [p, p + n) are known, whatever p is; print the known bytes as in the first case.

notes: No explicit loops in the source (functions and internals reached). The 10 whiles are 8 word copies of creation code / constructor arguments (P7) and 2 checked-exp loops. createTokenBridge (1,350 pack lines) reviewed by structure: create2 deployments with their salts, retryable-ticket calls, storage of the deployment, events; setTemplates / setDeployment / getters checked against the source. No semantic error found.
summary: Complete and faithful; no source loops. createTokenBridge is hard to follow because memory buffers are addressed by nested floor32/ceil32 sums and some salts hash raw memory; copies stay loops (P7).
